title: The Common's Due
tropes: the rule that must not be broken
the cost written on the body
logline: A miner bonded by debt to stake a rich new seam and the hedge-witch sworn never to charm past the boundary stones both need the same scrap of marsh ground to save, and neither can afford to pay what it costs.
promise: A hedge-witch's craft is shown doing real, respected work with a real price, and the prohibition laid down at the start is honored rather than broken, by a cleverer road than anyone expects.
setting: the grazing common between the Glasswood and the Hollowmere, in the Ashfall Marches, as the season turns toward the first hard frost

cast.name: Bram Tolliver
cast.want: to clear his debt by staking a workable claim before the solstice deadline, without anyone on the common paying the price for it
cast.dress: heavy boots, heavy trousers, long-sleeved shirt, neckerchief
cast.voice_note: plain and direct, slow to explain himself, quicker with his hands than his words

cast.name: Hazel Fenn
cast.station: hedge-witch to the grazing common, charming livestock and births for payment in kind
cast.want: to keep the common's cattle safe and her neighbours' trust without paying her teacher's price for breaking the rule
cast.appearance: a woman of twenty-seven with weather-reddened cheeks, a thick braid of light brown hair, and calloused hands
cast.dress: a wool shawl pinned over a patched herder's dress, with a pouch of charm-herbs tied at her belt
cast.voice_note: blunt and watchful, warms slowly, drops into old formulas of speech when she binds a charm

cast.name: Aldous Pike
cast.station: Ashfall camp foreman, holds Bram's tool-debt and answers to the Survey's own creditors
cast.want: to show a profitable claim staked before the solstice, whatever it costs anyone else
cast.appearance: a heavyset man of fifty-two with a grey beard and ink-stained fingers from years of ledgers
cast.dress: a long oilskin coat over a merchant's waistcoat, boots kept too polished for a mining camp
cast.voice_note: brisk, transactional, talks in numbers and deadlines

cast.name: Senna Loft
cast.station: elder holding the grazing rights to the common
cast.want: to keep the common and its herd safe, and to see old grudges against Hazel finally settled
cast.appearance: a stooped woman of sixty-three with white hair knotted at her neck and deep lines from sun and wind
cast.dress: a heavy wool cloak and a shepherd's crook she carries everywhere, worn smooth at the handle
cast.voice_note: dry, matter-of-fact, long memory for exactly who did what and when

chapters.title: A Seam and a Debt
beats: Bram surveys the marsh edge of the grazing common and finds a mineral seam rich enough to clear his tool-debt to Aldous Pike before the solstice deadline.
At the common he finds Hazel Fenn binding a charm-bundle of marsh herbs for a calf whose hide has begun to glow faintly under the ribs, from raw marsh plants taken up through its feed.

Hazel explains the boundary stones mark where marsh herbs are safe to gather and bind, and that her own teacher lost all feeling in her binding hand the one time she worked reagents taken from past that line.
She tells him the seam runs past the stones, warns him off, and refuses to help him survey further; Bram, with Pike's deadline pressing, crosses alone anyway.

chapters.title: Past the Stones
beats: Past the boundary, Bram confirms the seam is rich enough to clear his whole debt and more, and marks out the claim.
Returning, he finds a second calf sickening fast, its hide gone glassy at the ribs far quicker than Hazel has ever seen.
Senna Loft blames the digging talk itself for stirring the marsh, and says it is exactly what happened the year Hazel's teacher was hurt.

Hazel examines the calf, traces the sickness back toward Bram's new claim, and accuses him of cutting into something that should have stayed buried; Pike arrives delighted with Bram's numbers and moves the digging timetable up to three days hence.

chapters.title: What the Rock Carries
beats: Bram and Hazel compare his survey readings against her knowledge of the marsh plants and find the seam runs unbroken from deep marsh ground straight toward the common.
They test it together: Hazel binds a small dowsing charm from common-side herbs and walks the line with Bram's instrument, and both register the marsh's pull strongest exactly where the ore runs.

Bram realizes the vein is a channel carrying the marsh's influence outward, and that blasting it open to mine it would widen that channel, putting the whole common within the marsh's reach inside a season.

Hazel says the only way to seal the vein's throat without digging is to bind the ground over it with marsh-strength herbs gathered from past the stones, paying her teacher's price; Bram proposes moving the stones themselves instead.

chapters.title: The Line Redrawn
beats: Hazel objects that moving the stones is cheating the rule rather than keeping it; Bram argues the rule was set to keep raw marsh material off the common, not to fix two stones forever in one place.
Senna Loft admits a flood shifted one of the stones long before the Cataclysm and nobody minded then, which loosens Hazel's resolve.
They agree to try it that night, using winches and levers from Bram's kit to shift the two nearest stones a few yards, bringing the sick calf and the vein's throat inside a redrawn line.
Word comes from Pike that he has moved the crew's start time up again, to first light instead of midday, leaving them only the dark hours to finish.

chapters.title: First Light
beats: Working through the night, Bram levers the stones into their new places while Hazel keeps the frightened calf calm and gathers the herbs she needs from ground now inside the line.

Just as the sky greys, Hazel binds a charm over the calf and the ground together, and because the working is honestly on the common side now, the glow fades and the marsh's pull along the vein goes quiet, costing her nothing worse than a night without sleep.

Pike's crew arrives at first light ready to dig; Bram hands him a report naming the seam a hazard rather than ore, and offers to sell the finding to the joint Hollowmere survey instead, clearing his debt in credit.

Pike takes the deal rather than lose face with nothing to show; Senna tells the common the glow is gone and the old grudge against Hazel eases; Bram asks to help her set proper new markers along the whole line as the season's first true frost settles over the common.

notes: Set this story with the miner
